newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF AUXERRE PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF AUXERRE PLAYERS.

text.p: Pen pictures of the players most likely to turn out for Auxerre against Marseille in the French first division match at the Velodrome stadium on Sunday:

Fabien Cool, goalkeeper, age 22. Capable stand-in for Lionel Charbonnier, who was forced through injury to miss the decisive last European champions' league group match against Glasgow Rangers last week, a 2-1 home win, and the remaining domestic games before the winter break.
Alain Goma, defender, 24. Has been in fine form and won his first full French cap this season, but injury during training this week has put his participation in the match in doubt.
Frederic Danjou, defender, 22. Tall central defender who has shown considerable maturity in Auxerre's first European Cup campaign, seizing his chance due to Australian Ned Zelic's injury.
Taribo West, defender, 22. Nigerian international who helped his country win the Olympic title in August. A solid, versatile player who may play on the right if Goma is unavailable.

Franck Silvestre, defender, 29. Next to 30-year-old Charbonnier, oldest member of a young squad with an average age of 24 and a half. Experienced and very solid, he plays free just in front of back three or as stopper.
Franck Rabarivony, defender, 26. Left back who is quick going forward but can find himself in trouble when he has to deal with a fast winger like Ajax's Nigerian Tijani Babangida.

Eric Assati, defender, 22. Cool, Danjou and Assati are born within two days of each other in September 1974 and have come through together from the club's much admired youth scheme. He has slotted in well since being called upon for the tricky champions' league away match against Ajax Amsterdam.
Christian Henna, midfielder, 24. Tireless ball winner who was injured recently and is unlikely to recover in time for the match.

Antoine Sibierski, midfielder, 22. New recruit from Lille and one of a string of players who have missed matches through injury this season, but has probably recovered sufficiently to be in the reckoning.

Moussa Saib, midfielder, 27. Algerian captain who has been at Auxerre since 1992, he has been superb in the chief midfield role in the absence of injured Sabri Lamouchi and departed Corentin Martins. Club's top scorer in the league this season with six goals.

Sabri Lamouchi, midfielder, 25. French international whose ankle injury problems this season started when he was cut down playing for his country against Turkey in October. Captain and attacking midfielder who was expected to take over the mantle of Martins before injury. Could start on bench.
Philippe Violeau, midfielder, 26. Another busy midfielder who doubles for Sibierski or Lamouchi.

Steve Marlet, forward, 22. A big, fast, skilled runner on the ball who was recruited from second division Red Star. Injuries to team mates gave him a chance which he took in style by scoring the winning goal against Ajax in Amsterdam.
Abdelfahid Tasfaout, forward, 27. Algerian international who is a likely starter up front, particularly in absence of left wing Bernard Diomede.

Lilian Laslandes, forward, 25. A big centre-forward who is good at shielding and providing the ball for fellow attackers. He also has the knack of poaching goals. Injury put him out for two months, when he was ably replaced by Thomas Deniaud, but he has made a timely comeback. He has scored five league goals this season.
